findings.verdict: MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED. Cause identified by ablation and by an executable geometry audit, not by argument. Filed five times across four rounds; this is the first round it was localised to a line.

prediction.stated: BEFORE the fix: correcting the winding makes the card an up-facing Lambert surface, i.e. it is lit exactly as the flagstone it lies on. The foliage-absent capture measures those same boxes at p50 49.2 / detail 10.55 and p50 36.7 / detail 9.24, so a correctly-lit card of similar albedo lands near there.
prediction.guard_0.4949,0.8453: p50 41.3 must not move. STRUCTURALLY SAFE: that box is byte-identical between r17v1 and r17v2, i.e. NO foliage fragment lands in it at all, so nothing in my file can move it.
prediction.guard_frameP50: 75.8 +/- 8%. The lifted region is 22,769 px = 0.769% of the frame and lies below the median, so the median cannot move measurably.
prediction.falsifier: If the boxes come back still under 10, the winding was not the mechanism and the next thing to read is whether Props/Level draws something else at world XZ (-6.0, 38.2).

howItWasLocalised: 1. ABLATION, free and already captured. r17v1 has no foliage at all. The three void boxes read p50 49.2 / 36.7 and detail 10.55 / 9.24 there, against 3.1 / 3.4 and 2.54 / 4.02 in r17v2, while the critic's own guard box is byte-identical in both. The voids ARE foliage. The re-route was correct.

2. Connected-component analysis of 'foliage turned this pixel near-black' (v2 luma < 10 while v1 luma > 25): 22,769 px in hero, dominant component 9,242 px at bbox (1285,973) 210x93, centroid (1388,1016) -> world XZ (-6.12, 38.31), 10.3 m from the hero eye, footprint 2.6 x 2.8 m.

3. WHICH LAYER. Rasterised every foliage mesh's real instance buffer through the hero camera and intersected with that mask: ground-cards 95.1% (and it covers the centroid), grass-l0-b2 7.9%, susuki 5.6%, grass-l1-b1 3.5%, ferns 2.2%, grass-l2 0.0%, far-cover 0.0%. far-cover is independently dead here: its fadeIn is [28, 35] m against a 10.3 m patch, which confirms the coordinator's elimination.

4. WHY BLACK. An executable audit comparing each geometry's per-triangle GEOMETRIC normal ((b-a) x (c-a)) against its authored vertex normal, over every mesh in the group. ground-cards: 6 triangles, 0 agree, **6 OPPOSE**. Nothing else in the build has a fully antiparallel pair (far-cover 4/4 agree, grass-l2 4/4, bamboo-cards 4/4, tree-impostors 2/2).

mechanism.what: GeoBuilder.card(c, A, B, nrm, ...) winds its quad (c-A-B, c+A-B, c+A+B, c-A+B), so the geometric face normal is A x B. buildGroundCard passed A = r = (cos a, 0, sin a)*s and B = u = (-sin a, 0, cos a)*s, and r x u = (0, -s^2, 0). Every ground card's face was wound pointing DOWN, exactly antiparallel to the `up` normal authored on its own vertices.
mechanism.whyItWasSilent: The material is DoubleSide, so the card still rasterises and still alpha-tests correctly — the silhouette in the frame is right, which is why five rounds read it as a shadow or a decal rather than as the card itself. What breaks is shading: three's <normal_fragment_begin> negates the interpolated normal on a double-sided BACK face (`normal *= faceDirection`), and every camera in this build looks at a ground card from above, i.e. from the side its winding declares the back. So the fragment shades with N = (0,-1,0).
mechanism.arithmetic: dot(N, sunDir) with sunDir (0.86, 0.225, 0.457) is -0.225, clamped to zero: NO direct sun at any intensity. The hemisphere term samples the ground colour instead of the sky. The only light left is FRAGMENT_SSS's wrapped lobe at wrap = clamp((-0.225+0.55)/1.55) = 0.210, which is the residual the critic measured INSIDE the voids as luma 3.1 with a faint structure visible at 8x gain — not 'no texture inside', but the card's own moss/litter texture at ~0.001 linear.
mechanism.whyByteIdenticalAcrossBuilds: buildGroundCard has not been touched since it was written. Round 16 changed far-cover, round 17 changed bamboo; neither goes near it.
mechanism.whyItIsBELOW the fill floor: Round 15's 'fill-only plaza p50 21.0' is the floor for an UP-facing surface. A down-facing one does not get that floor, which is exactly why this patch was 7x darker than a legitimate cast shadow (p50 16.3) sitting 100 px away in the same crop.

findings.change: buildGroundCard now calls g.card([cx,y,cz], u, r, up, ...) — arguments swapped, so the cross product is u x r = (0, +s^2, 0). Verified by re-running the audit: 6 triangles, 6 agree, 0 oppose. It transposes the texture on the card, which is invisible: every instance is yawed at random.

1_theFlatGreenQuad.identification: It is `bamboo-canopy`, my far-field shell, and it covers 71.7% of that exact box.
1_theFlatGreenQuad.mechanism: RANGE.canopy declares the shell as the 110-900 m stand-in, and that was enforced ONLY as a world radius about the origin — never as a distance from the camera. Round 17 moved the valley eye to r = 112.00, two metres outside the shell's own inner rim.

A shell quad is about 7 x 6 m where it first survives the `below` test, so at 19-33 m it rasterises 250-300 px across: a straight-edged, untextured, flat dark-green facet. That is the finding, exactly.
1_theFlatGreenQuad.fix: A camera-distance dissolve in the canopy fragment shader over [70.4, 110.0] m — the far end is RANGE.canopy[0] itself, not a tuned number. World-space fbm threshold so the boundary is stable under camera motion and reads as a thinning stand rather than a ring. Costs 0 triangles and 0 draw calls; it does cost early-Z on that one mesh, which is the trade.

findings.verdict: PREMISE DISPROVED BY MEASUREMENT, and the real defect turns out to be the same one as the valley blocker. No fog change made, and none should be.

criticHypotheses.text: (a) the foliage material is not consuming the same fog/aerial term the terrain is
criticHypotheses.status: DISPROVED by source. `this.ctx.sky?.applyFog?.(mat)` is called on all three material factories in this file — _makeMaterial (line ~3384, which builds every bamboo, grass, fern, susuki, ground-card and far-cover material), _makeImpostorMaterial (~4641) and the canopy (~5292). And FRAGMENT_SSS is injected before <envmap_fragment>, which is before <fog_fragment>, so the transmitted lobe is fogged too.

criticHypotheses.text: (b) the term is keyed off a depth input the instanced card path does not write, so every card is evaluated at the camera's own depth
criticHypotheses.status: NOT THE MECHANISM, because there is nothing for it to be wrong about.

findings.theDisproof: The three boxes the finding is built on are not near, mid and far. Rasterising every layer's depth through the valley camera and taking the nearest visible surface per pixel: the 'near' box 0.0790,0.6667 is bamboo-card at 22 m (nearest 19), the 'mid' box 0.5727,0.5983 is bamboo-card at 28 m (nearest 22), and the 'far' box 0.7504,0.5128 is bamboo-card at **25 m** (nearest 22). All three are the same layer within six metres of each other. The critic inferred distance from apparent culm width (90 px vs 25 px), but the card band's instances vary 7-20 m in world height and each card is painted with several culms, so a small on-screen culm is a SMALL CARD, not a distant one.
findings.consequence: No aerial-perspective ladder can exist across a 6 m depth interval, and the finding's own p50 measurement (falling 6 codes over what it believed was a 3.6x scale ratio) is what you get when the three samples are at the same distance and differ only by which card they landed on. The frame does not lack fog; it lacks depth. That is finding 3, and the bamboo-card near-edge change above is the fix for both.
findings.prediction: After the near edge moves to 52 m, the three boxes stop being the same distance: the 'far' box should be looking at cards 60-170 m out or at the exposed valley wall. If the p50 ladder is still flat AFTER that, the finding becomes Sky's, and the instrument should be rewritten to sample boxes chosen by measured depth rather than by apparent culm width.

findings.verdict: PARTIAL. One half fixed structurally; the other half DISPROVED as reachable from this file, with the arithmetic.

criticHypotheses.text: whether the impostor is receiving the same aerial-perspective term as the terrain it stands on
criticHypotheses.status: DISPROVED. _makeImpostorMaterial calls this.ctx.sky.applyFog(mat) at line ~4641, the same call every other material in the file gets.

criticHypotheses.text: whether the impostor card is a single quad per tree with no crown silhouette at all
criticHypotheses.status: CONFIRMED, by the geometry audit: tree-impostors is **2 triangles**, i.e. one quad per tree. Its silhouette is entirely the baked alpha.

fixed.why: frameRel sizes the bake camera AND the card's world half-extent, so raising it widens both by the same factor: the tree keeps its world size and gains transparent margin. At 1.06 the crown's widest point sat at 0.94 of the half-cell, so on the azimuths where the crown is widest it reached the cell border and the atlas cut it WITH the border — a straight vertical alpha edge, which is precisely what the finding measures ('near-identical vertical lozenges, each with a binary alpha edge') and what its acceptance forbids ('no straight vertical alpha edge longer than 25 px'). At 1.22 the crown cannot reach the border on any of the 8 azimuths.
fixed.cost: 0 triangles, 0 draw calls. Texel density inside the cell drops to (1.06/1.22)^2 = 0.755 of a 256 px cell feeding a 40-80 px card — still 3x oversampled. Fill on the card goes up 32%.

notFixed_andWhy.theKnob: uChroma in _makeImpostorMaterial, currently 0.72. It mixes each fragment toward its own luminance: diffuseColor = mix(vec3(lum), diffuseColor, uChroma). Round 15 set it by measurement, against a sakura impostor at saturation 0.350 when the frame mean was 0.232.
notFixed_andWhy.disproof: Saturation as probe.mjs defines it, (max-min)/max, scales essentially linearly with this mix. Removing the pull ENTIRELY (uChroma 1.0) can therefore reach at most 0.085 / 0.72 = **0.118**, against the 0.15 acceptance — a 21% shortfall — while re-introducing exactly the over-saturated sakura impostor round 15 fixed by measurement. So I did not touch it: shipping a knob that provably cannot clear its own acceptance and reverts a measured fix is the failure mode this project's preamble is about. The residue is in the baked atlas's own colour (the bake runs under a neutral 2.35 white key with tone mapping off) and in the fog applied after it.
notFixed_andWhy.alsoNotReached: lumaSpread >= 70 (currently 44.6) needs a lit-top / shaded-underside break inside the impostor, which is a property of the bake's lighting rig, not of the frame margin. Not attempted this round.

findings.apparatusCaveat: I could NOT confirm from the harness that the `wide` band at (100,380 700x140) is tree-impostors: _scatterTrees places against the real splat and slope field, and my stub terrain is a radial profile with no hillside, so no impostor lands in that box offline. The identification rests on tree-impostors being the only distant tree layer in the build and on the critic's description matching a one-quad billboard atlas exactly. If the verification frame shows the band unchanged in silhouette, check first whether the band is terrain splat rather than my layer.

theMeasurement.reading: Card size fell 2.8x, clump count rose 8.6x and a hashed-alpha dither was installed, and the high-frequency energy in the crown moved -0.88 and +0.12. So the residual is NOT card size, NOT the floret scale on my sheet, and NOT the binary cutout — all three were changed together and measured. What DID move is the value distribution: box A's median rose 42 codes while its p99 did not move at all, i.e. the crown's shaded population climbed into its lit population and the internal value break collapsed. That is the shape of an emissive/ambient floor, and Props.blossomMaterial carries one (totalEmissiveRadiance += diffuseColor * (0.052,0.070,0.100) + (0.150,0.168,0.176) * skyView), which round 17 raised by +22.3% at the sphere mean.

openItems.item: The offline harness is worth committing to tools/.
openItems.detail: It is about 200 lines: a no-op Canvas2D shim, a stub ctx, and a rasteriser that walks the real instance buffers through a SHOTS camera. It located this round's blocker to a line, disproved a major's premise, and sized every change before it was made, without a browser or the rig lock. It needs a real terrain to be useful on valley — the radial profile I used is copied out of Cinematic.js's own documented ray-march along that shot's bearing, and the crude 'drop from r=80' version my predecessor used puts the valley eye 27 m above its own ground and makes every near-field raster read 0%.

openItems.item: GeoBuilder.card()'s winding contract is undocumented and has now cost one blocker.
openItems.detail: The geometric normal is A x B for arguments (A, B), and nothing says so. Every other caller happens to pass a vertical card whose authored normal is deliberately fake and roughly perpendicular to the face, so the sign never mattered; buildGroundCard was the one horizontal card, where the two could be exactly antiparallel. A cheap guard for a later round: assert at boot that no triangle's geometric normal opposes its authored vertex normal by more than 90 degrees on any single-sided-lit layer. The audit is fifteen lines and it is in this round's scratch.

openItems.item: sakura-wood, momiji-wood and cedar-wood also audit as 100% opposing (1280/1280, 868/868, 1904/1904).
openItems.detail: NOT investigated and NOT changed — out of scope for this round's findings, and unlike buildGroundCard these are closed tubes whose 'authored' normal is the outward ring normal, so the audit's verdict may be an artefact of how buildTree winds its own quads rather than a defect. Flagging it only because the round-18 critic describes the sakura branches as 'flat dark strokes drawn on top of the blossom mass', which is what an inside-out tube renders as, and because this file's own linkRings comment says exactly that: 'every culm and every trunk is built inside out and renders as an unlit black shell'. One command settles it; nobody has run it.
